note: EMPTY, and that is a statement about the 9 guards in tools/dev/anti-vacuity-cases.json. Swept 2026-08-30: 90 test files both scan the tree and derive a zero-verdict from it. Each was run under three lenses — blank the bound root; blank that root's test files too; blank EVERY root at once so no inferred binding can explain a pass — and every green was then checked for how much of the tree SURVIVED the blank. Result: 72 went red (proven non-vacuous), 3 throw when their corpus is absent (a guard refusing to report over nothing), 14 are outside the instrument's reach, and ONE was a real finding — no-leftover-backup-files, now fixed and in the manifest. The 14 are not suspects. Eight are refilled by their own import closure, the limit knobs-import-bundle is reported UNSUPPORTED for; three scan a temp directory they create themselves, so they have no repo corpus to be vacuous about; repo-index-hygiene derives every verdict from the git index and never reads the tree; the rest read a directory listing the blank cannot empty. This CORRECTS the previous note, which reported '16 more vacuous guards' from an interrupted partial sweep. Every one was a lens artifact: a single blanked root cannot tell 'the guard noticed nothing' from 'the root it actually reads was left standing', and the binding was inferred rather than known.
